title: A simple agent, end to end
lede: One builder, one wizard, one key, one agent: how a governed agent gets made and what happens on its first call.

edges.label: key created, selecting apps made the grant
Bearer key on every call, no sign-in
mcp scope and grant: tools listed and called
llm scope and allowlist: model reached
a failed check stops the call

steps.title: Register the agent
steps.what: The builder runs the Add Agent wizard: name, custodian, expiry, scopes, the apps or models it may reach, limits and AI Guard.
steps.why: Selecting the apps on the key is the grant; saving creates the grant policy for the custodian.

steps.title: The key is minted
steps.what: Step 4 of the wizard shows the key once, with calling code per scope. There is no rotate: rotation is delete and recreate.
steps.why: The key is the agent's whole identity, sent as a bearer token on every call.

steps.title: The agent holds the key
steps.what: The agent embeds the key in its calling code. It never signs in and never exchanges tokens.
steps.why: A revoked or expired key stops the agent instantly, without touching the code.

steps.title: Every call passes the gateway
steps.what: The gateway checks the key, scope, grant, limits and guardrail in order. The first failure refuses the call with a status code.
steps.why: The caller's key is never forwarded to a backend; the gateway decides before the target sees anything.

steps.title: Granted targets answer
steps.what: With the mcp scope the agent sees and calls only its granted tools; with the llm scope it reaches only allowlisted models within its caps.
steps.why: One agent, one key, deliberate reach: this is the demo's whole story in one walk.
